adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new gate for `optimized_pagination` using `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` (in `organization_auditlogs.py`). Whether `has_global_access` is overly broad in open-membership orgs, and whether `is_superuser` should be replaced by an “active superuser session” check, cannot be verified from this diff alone (it depends on those fields’ semantics elsewhere). However, the finding is a specific, diff-grounded concern about potentially incorrect authorization criteria for enabling the new advanced pagination path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — BasePaginator now clamps negative offsets for next cursors but still uses the original negative cursor.offset in build_cursor and in the `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check, and is_prev negative offsets still reach queryset slicing and 500 on every BasePaginator endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `BasePaginator.get_result` the new logic clamps negative `offset` only when `not cursor.is_prev` (`start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`). For `is_prev` cursors a negative `cursor.offset` will still be used directly in `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, and Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices (raises), leading to 500s if a negative offset is provided. The finding’s note that later logic still uses the original `offset` (e.g. `len(results) == offset + limit + extra`) is also true, since `offset` is unchanged even when `start_offset` is clamped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — zpopmin eviction silently drops spans with no metric or log, and the flush-side segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log was removed, so truncated segments are emitted as if complete

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds hard truncation in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` via `zpopmin` when `span_count > 1000`, which drops spans without any metric/log. At the same time, `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py::_load_segment_data` removes the previous `max_segment_spans` safeguard that emitted `segment_span_count_exceeded` metric/log and skipped oversized segments. As a result, segments can now be silently truncated in Redis and then flushed/emitted as if complete, representing silent data loss introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:449 — The flush-side span-count ceiling was removed, but the pipelined zadd into an already-queued segment key is unbounded until the later EVALSHA pipeline runs, so a concurrent flusher can zscan and flush a segment with far more than 1000 spans

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the flush-side span-count guard in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` (the `max_segment_spans` check and early skip were deleted) while `process_spans` now pipelines `ZADD` into `set_key` with no corresponding cap (`p.zadd(set_key, {...})`). Although `add-buffer.lua` enforces a hard cap of 1000 via `zpopmin`, that cap only applies in that Lua path; nothing in the shown Python `zadd` path prevents a sorted-set segment key from growing past 1000 spans. Therefore a flusher doing `zscan` can indeed flush a segment containing far more than 1000 spans if writers have appended many entries to that key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py:141 — val["end_timestamp_precise"]` is not validated, so a missing field raises KeyError and a null/NaN value makes ZADD fail, either of which aborts the whole batch and can crash-loop the consumer on one poison message

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `end_timestamp_precise` a required field in the consumer path by doing `end_timestamp_precise=val["end_timestamp_precise"]` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py) with no default/guard. If a message lacks that key, `KeyError` will be raised while building the batch, plausibly aborting processing and repeatedly failing on the same poison message. The new Redis storage path also uses this value as a ZSET score (`p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})`), so a non-numeric/NaN value could raise from the Redis command and similarly fail the batch. The diff shows no validation or exception handling around either use.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py:126 — Every test span uses the same end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0 and no test exceeds 1000 spans, so the eviction path and its end-time ordering are never exercised, leaving the suite green without testing the change

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds span eviction/trimming logic in `add-buffer.lua` (`if span_count > 1000 then redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000) end`) and changes span storage to a sorted set keyed by `end_timestamp_precise` (`buffer.py` uses `zadd(... {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise})`). In `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py`, all newly-added `end_timestamp_precise` values are the same constant `1700000000.0`, and the shown tests only create a handful of spans, so neither the `> 1000` eviction path nor score-based ordering behavior is exercised. This is a concrete missing-test/edge-case gap tied to newly introduced nontrivial behavior, not an immediately verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — ZUNIONSTORE uses the default AGGREGATE SUM, so a redelivered or duplicate span payload found in both keys gets its score doubled (and keeps growing on further duplicates), which corrupts the eviction order by making those spans effectively unevictable

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`, the diff replaces set unions with sorted-set unions via `redis.call("zunionstore", set_key, 2, set_key, span_key)` (and similarly with `parent_key`) without specifying `AGGREGATE`. Redis `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `AGGREGATE SUM`, so if the same span payload (member) exists in both `set_key` and the merged key (e.g. due to redelivery/duplication or repeated merges), its score will be added, inflating the timestamp-based score used for eviction (`zpopmin`). That distorts eviction order and can make frequently duplicated spans stick around longer than intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:62 — The hard-coded 1000 cap ignores the configurable max_segment_spans (default 1001), which is now dead config, so operators and tests tuning it get no effect

adjudication.rationale: The diff hard-caps the Redis span collection size in `add-buffer.lua` via `if span_count > 1000 then ... zpopmin(..., span_count - 1000) end`, while the Python-side enforcement based on `self.max_segment_spans` in `SpansBuffer._load_segment_data` was removed (the block that incremented `segment_span_count_exceeded` and skipped when `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans`). This makes the effective limit a fixed 1000 at write/merge time, regardless of any previously configurable `max_segment_spans` value, which is a concrete behavior/configurability concern introduced by the change. The claim about the default being 1001 isn't verifiable from the diff, but the hard-coded 1000 vs config-based limit issue is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:30 — The redirect-walk limit dropped from 10000 to 1000 as an unrelated change and its explanatory comment was deleted, so span trees deeper than 1000 now silently fragment into separate segments

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` changes the redirect-walk loop from `for i = 0, 10000 do` (with a comment warning about depth) to `for i = 0, 1000 do` and removes the explanatory comment. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — zpopmin evicts by lowest end_timestamp, so a segment/root span that ends before 1000+ of its descendants can be evicted, yielding flushed segments with no is_segment span despite hrs=1.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:47 — ZUNIONSTORE with set_key as both dest and source rebuilds the whole destination zset (O(N)+O(M log M) skiplist rebuild of up to 1000 multi-KB payloads) on every subsegment merge inside the blocking Lua script, costlier than the prior SUNIONSTORE and stalls the Redis shard for large segments.

The diff changes span buffers from Redis sets to sorted sets and replaces `SUNIONSTORE` with `ZUNIONSTORE` in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`:

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — ZPOPMIN returns every evicted payload into Lua memory only to discard it; ZREMRANGEBYRANK set_key 0 (span_count-1001) would trim without materializing the payloads.

The diff adds a trimming step in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`:
```lua
if span_count > 1000 then
    redis.call("zpopmin", set_key, span_count - 1000)
end
```
`ZPOPMIN` returns the removed members (and scores) to the Lua script; since the return value is not used, this materializes evicted payloads in Lua/Redis response handling only to discard them. A `ZREMRANGEBYRANK`-style removal would avoid returning the removed elements and is more efficient. This is a performance/efficiency issue rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:434 — ZSCAN in the flush path now returns and float-parses a score for every member even though the scores are thrown away, which adds wire bytes and client CPU on every segment load.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197 — Storing span payloads in a ZSET instead of a SET adds per-member skiplist node and score overhead in Redis (payloads over 64 bytes always force skiplist encoding), which raises buffer memory use across all buffered traces.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes span buffering from Redis SETs to ZSETs: `p.sadd(...)` becomes `p.zadd(set_key, {span.payload: span.end_timestamp_precise ...})` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`, and the Lua script replaces `scard/sunionstore` with `zcard/zunionstore` and adds `zpopmin` trimming. adjudication.rationale: The diff changes span storage for `span-buf:s:{...}:*` from Redis SETs to ZSETs: `buffer.py` replaces `p.sadd(set_key, ...)` with `p.zadd(set_key, {...})` (around line 197), and the Lua script similarly switches `sunionstore/scard/sscan` patterns to `zunionstore/zcard/zscan`. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua:63 — zpopmin silently evicts spans past a hardcoded 1000 with no metric or log, and the removed segment_span_count_exceeded check leaves max_segment_spans unused, so data loss can't be seen or configured.

The diff adds a hard cap in `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua`:

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — OptimizedCursorPaginator deliberately passes a negative cursor offset into a Django queryset slice, which always raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported") and returns an unhandled 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:880 — A user-controlled negative cursor offset is sliced straight into the queryset "to access data beyond normal pagination bounds". Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indices and raises an exception (commonly `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.`), and there is no error handling here to convert it into a `BadPaginationError`, so this can surface as an unhandled 500. `cursor.offset` is taken directly from the cursor (see `Cursor.__init__` casting to `int` with no validation), and the org auditlog endpoint can enable this paginator via `optimized_pagination=true` for privileged users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:182 — The shared BasePaginator now passes unvalidated negative offsets through on purpose for every endpoint when `is_prev` is set, and the comment wrongly calls this safe, instead of rejecting them with BadPaginationError (400).
